CANDOAREA: CEI SINCERI

ABNEGAȚIA: CEI ALTRUIȘTI

NEÎNFRICAREA: CEI VITEJI

PRIETENIA: CEI PAȘNICI

ERUDIȚIA: CEI INTELIGENŢI

Beatrice Prior se află în pragul unei decizii pe care fiecare persoană din lumea ei este obligată să o ia: cinci facţiuni, cinci viitoruri, cinci vieţi.

Ea are deja un plan: va face cea mai curajoasă alegere și va părăsi Abnegaţia pentru a se alătura Neînfricaţilor, chiar dacă asta înseamnă să-și abandoneze familia.

Însă atunci când o tragedie lovește în timpul ceremoniei de alegere, totul se schimbă – lumea ei, planurile ei, ba chiar și Beatrice însăși.

Decizia ei o va arunca direct în vizorul unei rebeliuni din umbră, unde un băiat cu secrete la fel de periculoase ca ale ei – un băiat care are drept nume doar o cifră – ar putea fi singura persoană în care poate avea încredere.

Pentru că, uneori, drumul pe care alegi să mergi nu îţi schimbă doar viitorul. Îţi schimbă întreaga lume.

I genuinely had SUCH A FUN TIME reading this. As a HUGE Divergent fan back in the prime time of YA dystopia - I was SO excited and so curious to see what this alternate reality version of the story would be like. I am so happy to say, it did not disappoint.

Don't want to say too much, but I will say Veronica Roth gave us the perfect balance of nostalgia + new material. We have a story that feels so true to the original, we have some of our favourite iconic moments interwoven into a completely new story. I was actually shrieking and giggling while reading parts of this book.

This version definitely gives us more insight into the different factions and how they operate, which I really appreciated. We immediately get more of an ominous political story, diving into the darker parts of this dystopia vs the original - where we started out a bit lighter, faster & easier if that makes sense. I can also very clearly see the improvements in Veronica Roth's writing since the original trilogy. The world building feels more nuanced and integrated into the story naturally, the characterization feels deeper. While all staying very true to the essence of the Divergent we love.

I will say... I'm UNSURE of something huge that happened at the end. Still muddling over it in my head, but I cannot make sense of it and the intention behind it. But I am very curious to see how book 2 progresses and cannot wait to finish the duology and see where we go from here!

All that to say, if you loved Divergent - definitely pick this one up! I NEED SOMEONE TO TALK TO ABOUT THIS!!!!

Going back into the world of Divergent was something I was both excited and nervous about. There is something about revisiting familiar characters and seeing how different choices can change their stories that really appealed to me. Tris is still fierce, determined and loyal to the people she loves, and I enjoyed seeing her face a different set of challenges. Four was another highlight, and their relationship was interesting to follow in this new version of events.

I liked getting another look at the factions and seeing how the story unfolds when things don't go as expected. I did feel that there was a lot happening at times, and some of the changes felt a little weird. While I enjoyed seeing familiar characters in different situations, I wasn't always convinced that every decision felt true to the characters I remembered, but I suppose people change when they face different decisions.

I'm glad I returned to this world, and I can appreciate what Veronica Roth was trying to do with a story that takes a different path from the original. I'm curious to see where the next book takes these characters, but this one left me with mixed feelings.

I finished The Sixth Faction feeling... meh. Underwhelmed, mostly. Not because I thought it was a terrible book, but because it was an okay book that ultimately disappointed me. And for a while, I couldn't quite figure out why something about it felt so off.

I think part of the problem is that I have a complicated relationship with Divergent and Veronica Roth's decisions regarding the series. I was genuinely traumatized by Tris's death in Allegiant, and I still strongly disagree with that ending. Then came We Can Be Mended, where Roth decided to pair Tobias with Christina, of all people. As if killing Tris wasn't enough! 😭 I hated that decision, too, and I wasn't alone in my reaction. What frustrated me even more was Roth's response to the backlash, particularly her suggestion that readers didn't have to consider the novella canon if they didn't want to.

I understand that authors have the right to make whatever creative decisions they want, even unpopular ones. But readers also have the right to criticize those decisions. And personally, I think Roth damaged the legacy of her own series with the choices she made.

So when The Sixth Faction was announced, I wasn't particularly excited. I questioned its existence before I even started reading it, and now that I've finished it, I'm still questioning it. Why revisit this universe after everything that happened? What was the point?

I'm a completionist, though. Once I start a series or become invested in a fictional universe, I want to read everything connected to it, and I don't DNF books. So naturally, I had to read this one, even if I wasn't particularly enthusiastic about it.

And I want to make something clear: I never expected this alternate universe to undo Tris's death or give me closure. I knew from the beginning that these were two completely separate universes. Roth herself has explained that they're separate, with differences extending beyond the characters' choices to the technology and certain cultural aspects of their worlds. This isn't the same Tris who died in Allegiant. That Tris is still dead. So seeing another version of her alive didn't make me particularly happy or emotionally connected to her.

I was willing to judge this alternate story for what it was. Unfortunately, I just didn't find it especially compelling.

The question I couldn't stop asking: Why does this book exist?

I actually looked into Veronica Roth's explanations for writing The Sixth Faction, hoping they might help me understand what she was trying to accomplish.

According to Roth, the project began as a playful writing exercise. Years of criticism surrounding Divergent, particularly the backlash to Allegiant, had negatively affected her relationship with her own work. She wanted to rediscover the joy of writing in that universe and stop feeling embarrassed about something she'd created when she was younger.

She chose an alternate universe because it gave her the freedom to experiment without being constrained by the original trilogy's continuity. She has also acknowledged that, as a more experienced writer, there were aspects of her original worldbuilding she wanted to improve.

At the same time, Roth has maintained that The Sixth Faction isn't an attempt to fix Divergent, and that she still stands by the original ending, even if her feelings about it have become more complicated over time.

I find that interesting, and a little frustrating.

On one hand, I understand the distinction between wanting to improve certain elements of an old story and wanting to correct the story itself. Those aren't necessarily contradictory intentions.

On the other hand, if you're revisiting a universe partly because you recognize weaknesses in your original writing, while repeatedly emphasizing that you're not trying to fix anything, I can understand why that explanation might sound somewhat defensive.

And honestly, I still question whether Roth is as satisfied with her original decisions as she says she is. That's my personal impression, not something I can claim to know about her actual feelings.

Apparently, writing this book helped her rediscover her love for Divergent, and she has said that the project accomplished that personal goal.

Well, I'm glad she found her joy again. But an author's personal satisfaction with a creative experiment doesn't automatically make the resulting book worthwhile for readers.

If the original purpose was personal, I can't help wondering why that experiment needed to become a published story. Maybe she hoped revisiting the universe would rekindle readers' love for it, too. I don't know.

But it certainly didn't do that for me.

After Allegiant and We Can Be Mended, I honestly think Roth should have left Divergent alone. To me, this feels like beating a dead horse.

And the problem isn't simply that I didn't want another Divergent book. It's that Roth chose to revisit this universe, but the result didn't convince me that revisiting it was worthwhile.

Understanding why she wanted to write it hasn't changed that feeling.

The same story, but different

One of my biggest problems with The Sixth Faction is that it feels simultaneously familiar and different, but not necessarily in ways that make it better.

The alternate universe is somewhat interesting, and I appreciated some of its differences. But nothing about it felt particularly groundbreaking.

The core concepts remain largely intact, including the factions, and the story follows essentially the same general direction as the original trilogy.

Tris makes a different choice, encounters mysteries surrounding her society, discovers unsettling information, becomes involved in conflicts between factions, and finds herself caught up in events involving familiar characters and threats.

The details change, sometimes considerably, but the overall trajectory feels recognizable.

And that's where I struggled.

An alternate universe offers so many possibilities. You can explore how different circumstances reshape familiar characters, change the direction of major events, or examine entirely different consequences of the same underlying ideas.

But here, I often felt like I was reading a variation of something I'd already experienced, rather than discovering a genuinely compelling alternative.

It was different enough to remind me that these weren't the characters I originally knew, but similar enough that I couldn't stop comparing their stories.

And those comparisons became frustrating.

I actually had the original Divergent open while reading The Sixth Faction, partly because I wanted to compare certain details. But something unexpected kept happening: I'd start reading the original and become so absorbed in it that I'd forget about The Sixth Faction.

That says a lot about my experience.

The original has something that immediately captures my attention and makes me want to keep reading. This version never managed to recreate that feeling.

I was constantly conscious of reading an alternate version of Divergent. I never became so immersed that I forgot about the original.

Of course, alternate-universe stories naturally invite comparisons. I don't think comparing the two is inherently unfair. But ideally, those comparisons should make the alternate story more interesting, not constantly remind me of what I find lacking in it.

And unfortunately, that was often my experience here.

Following breadcrumbs without a satisfying payoff

The plot itself was okay. Not terrible, not particularly impressive.

My reading experience was inconsistent. Sometimes something interesting would happen and I'd become invested, only for the story to become boring again. Then another development would catch my attention, followed by another stretch that didn't particularly engage me.

It was a constant cycle of interesting, boring, interesting, boring.

And I think a lot of that had to do with how the mystery unfolded.

The entire book felt like following a trail of breadcrumbs.

Tris discovers something strange, like a bullet. She asks someone about it, which leads to another question. Then she goes to someone else, notices something suspicious, follows another person, overhears something she doesn't fully understand, and discovers another small piece of information.

And on and on it goes.

Now, there's nothing inherently wrong with a mystery built around gradually uncovering clues. That structure can be incredibly engaging when the discoveries build toward satisfying revelations.

But here, I kept waiting for those breadcrumbs to lead somewhere more substantial.

I wanted that moment when everything finally starts coming together, when you understand what was really happening and why.

Instead, I reached the end still feeling like I was missing too many pieces. I didn't fully understand everyone's motivations, the complete plan, or why certain characters had done what they did.

And yes, I know this is the first book in a duology.

I'm perfectly aware that some mysteries are intentionally being saved for the sequel. That's not my complaint.

A first installment doesn't need to answer every question, but it should reveal enough to make the journey satisfying while leaving you excited to discover more.

There's a difference between finishing a book thinking, I can't wait to find out what happens next! and finishing it thinking, Wait, that's all we're getting?

Unfortunately, my reaction was closer to the latter.

And despite all those unanswered questions, I'm not particularly excited about the sequel. I'll read it because I'm a completionist and don't like leaving things unfinished, not because this book left me desperate for more.

For a story that spends so much time building mysteries, that's disappointing.

Tris and Tobias were surprisingly the best part

Now, here's something I genuinely didn't expect.

My favorite part of The Sixth Faction was the relationship between Tris and Tobias.

I really wasn't expecting to enjoy their interactions as much as I did, especially considering my feelings about the original trilogy's ending and everything that followed.

But I did.

There was something genuinely lovely about watching these alternate versions of Tris and Tobias find each other.

Even in a different universe, under different circumstances, with different experiences shaping who they are, they still end up together.

And I love that.

Their interactions were probably the most consistently enjoyable aspect of the book for me. While the larger plot struggled to keep me invested, their relationship offered something I could actually appreciate.

It's interesting because Roth has mentioned enjoying the experience of writing Tris and Tobias together again, and that enthusiasm seems to have translated into one of the stronger elements of the story.

I also have to mention Christina.

After We Can Be Mended, I was practically triggered the moment Christina and Tobias appeared on the page together. 😂 I still haven't recovered from Roth pairing them up in that novella, so seeing them in the same story immediately brought back those memories.

Thankfully, Roth didn't have them interact very much.

Although, of course, Tris does briefly wonder whether there might be something more between them.

I suppose that was a little nod to the original universe and what eventually happened there.

Small mercies, I guess.

I'm just glad Roth didn't decide to revisit that particular relationship in any meaningful way.

And while I enjoyed seeing Tris and Tobias find each other again, I'm not getting too comfortable. Considering Roth's history with these characters, I genuinely wonder whether she'll kill Tris again in the sequel.

Hopefully not.

But then again, maybe she'll kill Tobias instead. At this point, who knows? 😭

Caleb's death: A shocking twist that didn't work for me

This was probably my biggest problem with the actual story.

Tris killing Caleb to save Tobias felt so completely out of left field that my immediate reaction was basically, Wait, WHAT just happened?

I understand the situation Roth created. Caleb was threatening Tobias, and Tris was forced into an impossible choice.

I also understand what Roth seemed to be exploring: a version of Tris who ultimately chooses romantic love over her family, making a dramatically different decision from the Tris we knew in the original trilogy.

But understanding what an author is trying to accomplish doesn't mean I find the execution convincing.

And I didn't.

We're talking about Tris killing her own twin brother to save a guy she's known for what, two or three months?

I know Tobias wasn't just some random guy to her, and I understand that Caleb posed an immediate threat. But the decision still felt unbelievable to me.

Maybe I could have accepted it if the circumstances and relationships had been developed differently. If Roth had spent more time building toward that moment, perhaps it would have felt like a tragic but believable culmination of this Tris's character arc.

Instead, it felt like Roth wanted to deliver a huge, shocking twist without doing enough to earn it.

And what makes it even more jarring is the contrast with Allegiant.

In the original trilogy, Tris literally sacrifices herself after taking Caleb's place on a mission they know is fatal.

Despite everything that happened between them, despite Caleb's betrayal, she ultimately chooses to take his place.

In The Sixth Faction, she kills him.

I understand that these are different versions of Tris, shaped by different experiences and circumstances.

But different doesn't automatically mean better, and a dramatic departure from the original doesn't automatically make for compelling character development.

To me, this wasn't a fascinating exploration of how different circumstances could change Tris. It was a decision that didn't feel sufficiently believable or emotionally earned.

And then there's the timing.

Caleb dies practically at the end of the book. Within roughly three chapters, the story is over.

We're talking about Tris killing her own twin brother, one of the most significant decisions she could possibly make, and there's barely any room left to explore the emotional consequences.

I wanted the story to give that moment the weight it deserved.

Instead, it felt like an enormous event introduced for shock value, followed by an ending that arrived before I could properly process what had happened.

The problem wasn't simply that Roth made Tris do something shocking. It's that the story didn't convince me that this version of Tris would make that choice, or give me enough time to feel the full impact of it afterward.

And that's a shame, because the contrast between the two versions of Tris could have been one of the most interesting aspects of the entire alternate-universe concept.

An interesting idea doesn't necessarily make a compelling book

I think this is where everything starts coming together for me.

The Sixth Faction isn't a terrible book. It has interesting ideas, some enjoyable moments, and a relationship I genuinely liked.

But the more I think about it, the more I feel that the book's biggest weakness is that it never gave me a compelling enough reason to care about this particular version of the story.

The alternate universe was interesting, but not especially original. The plot was okay, but followed a familiar direction. The mystery kept introducing new questions without providing enough satisfying answers. The pacing was inconsistent, and the biggest twist felt more shocking than believable.

And although I liked Tris and Tobias, their relationship wasn't enough to make the overall experience particularly memorable.

There's also an interesting contradiction in how I experienced the book.

The story was too similar to the original to feel genuinely fresh, yet some of its biggest departures felt too extreme to be convincing.

I think that explains a lot of my dissatisfaction.

It's not that I wanted Roth to rewrite Divergent exactly as it was. I already have that story, and despite my feelings about its ending, I still appreciate what made it compelling.

But if you're going to revisit an established universe and explore an alternate version of its characters, I want those differences to feel meaningful. I want to understand what this new version brings to the table.

And by the end, I still wasn't convinced that The Sixth Faction had brought enough.

Perhaps that's why I kept finding myself more interested in the original book whenever I opened it for comparison.

The original Divergent has a sense of momentum and emotional investment that this one never managed to recreate for me.

And that's especially disappointing when Roth has openly discussed wanting to revisit the universe with the experience and skills she's gained as a writer.

I understand that she's grown as an author, and I don't doubt that she approached this project with genuine enthusiasm. But being a more experienced writer doesn't automatically mean that a new version of an old story will be more compelling than the original.

For me, it wasn't.

My complicated feelings about Veronica Roth

I also think it's important to acknowledge that my history with Roth's books influenced my experience.

I went into The Sixth Faction carrying years of disappointment over Allegiant and We Can Be Mended. I wasn't excited about returning to this universe, and I couldn't completely separate those feelings from my reading experience.

But I don't think that automatically invalidates my criticisms.

After all, I still found things to enjoy. I genuinely liked Tris and Tobias's interactions, and there were moments when the mystery caught my attention.

So it's not as though I'd decided beforehand that I was going to hate everything about the book.

I gave it a chance, and it simply didn't win me over.

What frustrates me about Roth's approach to Divergent is that I sometimes get the impression she wants readers to appreciate her creative decisions without fully understanding why certain choices were so upsetting to them.

I know that's only my impression, and I can't speak for her actual feelings or intentions.

But from my perspective, she made decisions that deeply damaged my relationship with a series I once loved, and her subsequent attempts to revisit that universe haven't repaired it.

I also recognize that she doesn't necessarily owe readers that repair. She doesn't have to change her mind about Tris's death, and she doesn't have to write the story I would have preferred.

But equally, I don't have to appreciate every creative decision she makes simply because it's meaningful to her.

And that's ultimately how I feel about The Sixth Faction.

I'm glad writing it helped Roth rediscover her love for Divergent. But her personal experience with the project doesn't change my experience reading it.

To me, this feels like a universe that should have been left alone after We Can Be Mended.

And if Roth was going to revisit it anyway, I wish she'd given us something more compelling than a weaker variation of the original story.

Final thoughts

Ultimately, The Sixth Faction was an okay book that disappointed me, rather than a genuinely bad one. I enjoyed certain moments, especially Tris and Tobias, but I finished it feeling... meh. Underwhelmed.

The original Divergent made me want to keep reading. The Sixth Faction made me want to finish reading.

After everything, I'm still left with the same question:

Why did this particular story need to be told?

I understand why Veronica Roth wanted to write it.

I just wish she'd given me a better reason to want to read it.

Este libro es todo lo que podría pedir.

Estoy todavía procesando como escribir esta reseña, pues jamás en mi vida pensé que estaría hablando de un nuevo libro de Divergente. Spin off, secuela, segunda serie, Universo Alterno, lo que sea. Pensé que la puerta hacia este mundo se había cerrado con Leal, y a diferencia de muchas persona, al menos yo sí estaba satisfecho con eso. Aprendí a adorar la historia con los elementos que no me gustaron, con lo que sentía respecto a ciertos personajes, incluso con el final odiado que al menos a mi me parecía poético.

Entonces, obviamente cuando se anuncia este libro, y se nos platica el concepto, lo primero que pensé es "no lo quiero".

La idea de "reescribir" Divergente me encontró automáticamente en negación, pues creo que no era necesario en lo más mínimo. He seguido de cerca a Veronica Roth desde que empecé a involucrarme en las redes literarias entonces me consta la relación agridulce que tiene con este trabajo, pero me daba miedo que el escribir Divergente partiendo del mismo punto que la serie original pero tomar decisiones distintas de cierta manera estaría eliminando todo lo que la historia significa para mi. Pero puedo decir que ese no es el caso.

La Sexta Facción es un intento exitoso en darle una segunda vida a la historia que ya conocemos de Divergente. Desde un inicio lees a una Veronica Roth mucho más experimentada, más en sintonía con sus palabras y sus habilidades, por lo que el mundo de Chicago explota en tu cabeza de una manera que no habíamos leído antes. Descripciones más detalladas, un world building más exuberante y complejo (que en vez de alejarse de lo que ya conocemos agrándese y profundiza mucho más en el sistema de facciones, la corrupción de estos y el hilo que inevitablemente terminan uniendo a los que no pertenecen a ninguna), y personajes que se sienten como aquellas personas que conocimos hace muchos años pero traen algo distinto en ellos.

Este libro creo que nivela muy bien ambos factores: le da su espacio a los elementos originales de la historia, los honra, reconoce donde es que está el corazón de Divergente y, al mismo tiempo, cambia el juego lo suficiente para que también como lector sientas que esta nueva serie sí tiene un valor nuevo. Fue divertidísimo estar leyendo escenas icónica ahora volteadas, ver los pequeños cambios que brillan por su novedad y por lo bien que quedan dentro del escenario de la historia (Tris y Caleb son gemelos aquí? Likeee eso es buenísimo!), y también fue lindísimo para mi el poder seguir viendo y rocordando el porqué adoro esta historia con mi vida.

Desde un inicio YO me prometí que, pasara lo que pasara, iba a llegar a este libro con la mente abierta, que iba a tener la perspectiva de no permitir que la trilogía original sesgara esta nueva serie y que iba a hacer lo mejor para tenerlas separadas, por el simple hecho de darle una oportunidad justa a este libro. Y déjenme decirles que no fue necesario todo ese rollo; La Sexta Facción, estos nuevos Tris y Cuatro, la nueva rebelión y conflicto y todo dentro de este libro se defiende por si mismo.

Eso, para mi, ya es un éxito inmediato.

Al igual que en el primer libro original llega un momento donde la trama se detiene un poco para darle paso a la cementación del conflicto. Conocemos más de las facciones, de los conflictos internos dentro de estas y también de las relaciones detrás de escena entre los líderes que, poco a poco, se van mostrando más siniestras. Como les dije en un inicio, de verdad que la construcción del mundo aquí es impresionante. Hay tanto Lore nuevo de las facciones que ahora viéndolo en retrospectiva hace que se sienta que siempre estuvo incompleto hasta este momento. Es tan rico en desarrollo, en caracterización, que la idea de las facciones se siente más reforzada que nunca. Sí gracias a esto el libro se vuelve un poquito lento en partes pero es un Happy Problem.

Lo único medio "negativo" que diría de aquí es que para mi el romance se siente un poco menos desarrollado. A ver, ya conocemos a Tris y Cuatro, ya sabemos hacia donde van las cosas, pero justamente debido a las decisiones diferentes que se toman tenemos a dos protagonistas que no estan juntos gracias a la facción, por lo que sus encuentros son más esporádicos y tampoco cuentan con la proximidad que tenían al ser instructor + alumna, y por eso creo que como se va formando la pareja no se me hace con el tiempo y espacio suficiente. La sentí como muy rápido, chance me habría gustado que se esperara al segundo libro, o mínimo con más tiempo entre los dos para sí sentir que están cayendo el uno por el otro.

En fin, estoy inmensamente feliz de que este libro exista, de que me haya encantado, de haberle dado la oportunidad. No puedo esperar a Febrero para tener The Last Testimony y ver hacia donde va todo! Tengo muchas teorias de lo que podría cambiar Veronica Roth y sea lo que decida hacer yo lo voy a recibir con los brazos abiertos.

WE ARE SO FUCKING BACK!

-------

Un nuevo libro de Divergente en el año de nuestro señor 2026... Creo que jamás habíamos estado tan de vuelta.

Tengo mis dudas por el concepto, pero el libro preordenado está, y el 6 de octubre de 2026 a las 12:01AM empiezo este sin falta.

Prepárense para estar HARTOS de mi.

was this as good as the original? no, but i DON’T CARE! i’m just glad to be back in my divergent era! i didn’t know what to expect going into this book. in fact, i was SCARED, but i had nothing to be scared about! this book was fantastic and super intriguing! it absolutely has the divergent magic that i missed immensely.

the plot!! 🤝
what would be different about divergent if tris didn’t pick dauntless? what if she just….. decided to stay in abnegation, even though it clearly isn’t the right choice for her? i mean, we all know she’s meant to be dauntless, but that’s not what she chooses this time. what would happen? who would she meet? would she still befriend the same characters? would she still meet four?

as i already said, this was INTRIGUING!! divergent was the first dystopian series i ever read, so it means a lot to me. i mean, i even have an allegiant poster in my room. this book was like a breath of fresh air for me. it was like coming home. it was like being 13 again.

the characters!! 🔥
now, this is going to be a bit of a spoiler, but we meet a lot of the characters that we already knew from the old series, but we also meet some new ones. four (the love of my life) is just as amazing as ever. i mean, how could he not be? he’s four! he’s the blueprint!

tris was definitely an interesting character this time around. we see her making choices we know she shouldn’t be making, and that’s aggravating, but it’s supposed to be aggravating! this is practically fanfiction, people! it’s supposed to be different! it’s supposed to be plot twisty! get used to it! anyways, in the end, she gets right where she’s supposed to be, and that’s all that matters.

the ending!! 👁️

i’m totally looking forward to the next book! i’m excited to see how different it’s going to be from insurgent and allegiant. i just hope that you-know-who doesn’t you-know-what at the end because i will LOSE IT AGAIN!!!! i remember when i read that in allegiant, i was sick in bed and home alone. it was AWFUL! i cried SO BAD!! anyways, let’s not do that again.

would i recommend this book? ✨
yes!! don’t read this if you haven’t read the divergent series first of course, but if you have, don’t be scared to read this! it’s so good and so fun to experience the same story in a different way!

would i read it again? ✨
i would!! i could live in the divergent world forever. amity for life!

Review of advance copy received from Publisher
September 13, 2026
Thank you to Harper Collins and Veronica Roth for the proof in exchange for an honest review.

MINOR SPOILERS AHEAD - NOTHING FOR THE STORY THOUGH.

We return to the ruined Chicago in this AU version of Divergent where the premise is - what if Tris didn't choose Dauntless? After an attack during the Choosing ceremony, Tris decides not to join Dauntless, instead she makes a different kind of a choice.

Listen, I love myself a good AU. I think they're a fun way to explore different dynamics and once again meet the characters you love and have missed. And it has been quite a few years since I ventured into the Divergent world (so much so, I've unhauled the books from my shelves). This time, however, we have more than just Tris' POV as we venture into the story, we have two others - Four's and Caleb's.

Honestly, Caleb's POV, with how limited it was, felt useless. We got like 5 chapters of it, and that was it. I think I would have preferred a POV, if it's in such limited quantity, from one of the adult's. Natalie Prior, Janine or even Eric. Make me understand why they believe things they do. Why are they acting this way? Why these choices? Caleb just felt shoehorned in because the last time we had a dual POV from Tris and Four, we all know how that ended...

I also had a major issue with some inconsistencies in the story. During the Choosing ceremony, through a speech, it is established that the archaic beliefs like religion, were shed to create the faction system, and that is one of the reasons it functions. However, constantly on many many occasions, Tris talks about Abnegation's religious ceremonies. How can you have religious ceremonies, if the concept of religion was eradicated? Also, when Tris "swears" with words like "goddamn" etc, she does call it swearing, which would only count that way, if you do believe in a religion and think such words are blasphemous... but religion was shed, as were politics and other systems... so, which is it? It seems like such a small, tiny inconsistency, however, I couldn't help but see it, and it kept bugging me. I'm not saying that swearing the same way we do in our world would be eradicated, but the words would not hold the same kind of meaning, if they don't have the same worldly tether and context.

I think also reading this story at the age of 27, makes me realise how little the set-up of the Divergent world makes sense as a whole, that I could not see when I was a teen, so I was hoping that with certain tweaks and with time having passed since the original trilogy came out, Roth would have found a better way to explain why having only one personality trait and sectioning the city off in that way, was a good idea. But no... you have a whole AU to retcon and shape reasonings, and yet I feel like it was wasted. A book about how Divergent came to be would have been a more interesting read.

Ultimately, AUs are about changing things. It's about making different choices and seeing a different outcome. But this book, unfortunately, isn't that, and left me with a very big, unanswered question - who is this story even for?

Mainly, because not a lot changes compared to the first book. We sort of end up at the same place where we ended up in Divergent with the characters. And if that is the case, then what is the point of this story even existing?

Is this nostalgia-bait? Is this Veronica Roth trying to fix the universally hated ending of Allegiant? Is this a cash-grab because we're getting more of The Hunger Games, and she's seeing dystopia getting back on the top of YA genres?

The Hunger Games is giving us new stories, new things and concepts to think about, reshaping what we thought we knew and shedding new light on the darker corners. It is a series that has something to say.

But this cannot be compared to Hunger Games, because we're meeting all of the same characters at the same starting point, and our perception is not being changed of them. We're not getting a new perspective of what we already knew or thought we did, like we did in Sunrise on the Reaping and Haymitch with his games. In The Sixth Faction, the characters are the same, motivations are the same, and arcs are the same, it's just been given a different packaging with a slightly different ingredient list.

Overall, I am a bit sad, because I am unsure as to why this book has been written. I feel like there really isn't a reason for it to exist, because not much changes with the character and the arcs felt about the same how it did in Divergent. But maybe in the second book of this AU, it will be answered. I will read it once it comes out, because I do wish to see if it leaves me feeling like all of this had a point. Currently though, no. It feels like it doesn't, and I'm very sad to say so.

"Factionless isn't the worst thing I can imagine, not anymore. It's living a life that isn't mine."

Hey so this book had no right to make me near tears 92357237 times??? This was genuinely spectacular and I absolutely LOVED every single aspect of this book. I cannot wait for the sequel!!!

The Sixth Faction is truly such a marvelous book. I read Veronica's blog posts talking about how she was able to rediscover her love for the Divergent world writing TSF and it genuinely made me emotional reading those because you can really feel everything she went through since it's release and just how much TSF means to her, which made me love it even more. And it really shows how much fun she had writing this.

"But if you change the historical record, you can shape people's understanding of the present. And if you shape their understanding of the present, you can change society itself. Who's in charge. Who's to blame. Who's the enemy."

I reread Divergent before jumping into TSF and oh if it wasn't so much fun spotting the differences and similarities between both worlds. The way we got to see so many iconic scenes from the original series and not one thing in TSF felt repetitive--it somehow felt new while being nostalgic. And I love how Veronica expanded into the worldbuilding and plot right from the beginning and delved more into the political aspects like YES (it's hilarious because I always thought of Erudite as the only evil/insane ones in book 1 but oh boy...). I had enjoyed my reread of Divergent but you can immediately tell how much she's grown as an author since that era and the way she expands into SO much was such a blast. The relationships between specific characters had to be my favourite part about this book because omg they were amazing I love so many of them😭 We get more of Tris's relationship with her parents (like !!!), Four's relationship with his friends from Dauntless, and OF COURSE between Tris and Four! (which I will get into more later on in this review) And so many more well-written relationships but those would be spoilers if I mentioned specifics so you'll just have to read it for yourself ;)

"I think caring about them doesn't mean I owe them a version of myself that isn't real."

Tris was an absolute delight. I loved her in Divergent but believe it or not, she's even more amazing in TSF. No amount of words would ever be able to express how much I adore her. I genuinely just love being in her head so so much. Watching her internal struggles from the beginning to the insane events that kept happening around her and to her?? The amount of times my jaw dropped?? And then the gradual development in her character as she experiences so many different things... no because genuinely I can't explain how much I loved the realizations she came to and the freedom she felt. LIKE YEAH THAT'S MY GIRL. I was cheering so much. I love how much more confident Tris is here in comparison to the original book--like it makes sense why because of everything but oh if it wasn't so satisfying to witness. Also please, someone give Tris a hug. Protect her from this world!!!!

AND FOUR!!! Oh my gosh it 100% helped that we got his POV like that was the greatest blessing to come from this book🥹 I LOVED being in his mind. His relationship with Shauna and Zeke was actually everything. Four acting silly with them??? Oh my heartt I loved the friendship so much. And then we see his loneliness and how he doesn't have that sense of belonging with the Dauntless and it was SUCH an interesting perspective to see! Seeing his vulnerability so early on and the little details that we never knew in Divergent was just !! Like wow omg?? You really get to understand Four on a deeper level and I loved it. And of course he's the sweetest as always🥹 (side note: when they had their first kiss and Four was the one who was so giddy and smiling a lot to himself omg it was so cute!!)

"But he looks at me like I'm not seeing the whole picture. Like instead of not being enough of all those things, I'm actually more."

Which brings me to the romance. THE ROMANCE GUYS. Tris and Four are really looking to be one of my fav couples why are they so cute they actually have no right to be this adorable !! Divergent had insta-love and while I didn't mind it too much in my reread (because most books back then had it so its like whatever), I was SO happy to see that their relationship here felt wayyy more natural!! No insta-love here! The initial distrust because of the circumstances they meet in to respect and awe as they discover more about the other to trusting and finding comfort with the other and then those feelings growing more and more- yeah it was everything. I love the idea that in every universe they'll find each other and fall in love, like that's soulmates right there. They're so silly and cute, I kept grinning like an idiot. I can't wait to see how their relationship grows from here (AND DON'T KILL EITHER OF THEM PLEASE).

Then the other characters!! Caleb had his own POV chapters (I was shocked) and though there weren't many, it was so interesting seeing his perspective on some things. It's actually amazing how often my feelings on him kept changing. One thing for sure though I totally didn't expect a certain thing regarding his character oh my gosh. We see Christina again and GUYS I ADORE HER???? I know majority of the fandom disliked Christina in Divergent but she rocked here. Absolute queen, I need more of her. Then there were some new characters from the factionless who were awesome (shoutout to Rory and Colin!!) and I really hope it stays that way. Extremely curious about how things will turn out with them after how this book ended!! And then of course there were not so great characters... many in which I wanted to punch and unfortunately they were just as awful here as they were in Divergent... and it's also crazy how certain people still had the same things happen to them even in an alternate universe like damn😭 I really love how different this book is while feeling the same.

I am still reeling over that ending (seriously my heart was racing so fast) because WOW did those take some turns I did not expect??? The last one especially!!! I'm both relieved but sad for Tris, someone give this girl a break fr😭 I'm actually going to die (again) if The Last Testimony ends the same way as Allegiant LIKE PLEASE NO I'VE ALREADY BEEN TRAUMATIZED ONCE. I have no clue which direction this story will take next and it both thrills me and terrifies me. I've never been more glad that the sequel releases in February.
